assets.notes: gltf-transform weld -> simplify --ratio 0.0099 --error 0.06 (same ratio as ADR-0070's dragon decimation, not ADR-0074's 0.08 — this source has ~4-5x the triangle count of the 7 castle_* originals, so the same 0.08 ratio would have overshot the desktop triangle budget target; 0.0099 lands this file in the same final triangle range those 7 did) -> resize 512x512 (source had two 4096x4096 PNGs, ADR-0070 precedent for a textured source) -> prune pass on dragon_reference_v1 (mislabeled asset, see its own manifest note — real content is a fantasy castle/gatehouse with keep/twin corner towers/conical roofs/a wooden drawbridge, not a dragon). Assigned to the `twin` kingdom seat (DECISIONS.md ADR-0086) — the model's own drawbridge/gatehouse silhouette fits the Twins' river-crossing toll flavor already in `dialogueChoices.js`'s `twin-guard-1` entry. `hasMaterial: true` unlike the other 7 decimated castle entries: this source came with a baked PBR texture (unlike those 7's geometry-only Meshy originals), but `world/settlements.js`'s `spawnRealCastleModels` overwrites every loaded model's material with the same seeded `createStoneMaterial` regardless — the baked texture ships in the file (harmless, ~1MB) but is not actually rendered, same as it would be discarded if stripped instead. Real, deterministic stone material applied at runtime, not the baked one.
